subject: Bound startup, source-identity checks, atlas persistence and final descriptor close

sources.license: Apache-2.0; the existing PLE module retains its MIT provenance
sources.use: Original extension of existing local bounded-worker ownership; no new external implementation copied. Earlier peer design precedent and source/license details remain in peer-survey-io-resilience-20261015.json.

supersedes_limits: The item 1 startup inventory, live source-identity stat, atlas/trace flush and final descriptor-close exceptions in the original repair ledger.

The startup and ordinary-close synchronous filesystem exceptions in peer-survey-io-resilience-20261015.json and peer-survey-apc-metadata-accounting.json, for the production cache/streaming/PLE/atlas paths named here.
modifications: Reuse the fixed daemon ReadPool for bounded host-only control calls. A timeout revokes consumption while retaining the worker, its arguments and descriptor owner; replacement pools remain refused while abandoned work drains.

Give each existing pool at most one daemon finalizer, with a bounded caller wait. A blocked or failed final close retains ownership and blocks replacement; repeated close never retries an uncertain descriptor number. No device cleanup runs in the finalizer.

Move APC path resolution, directory security, lock acquisition, manifest inventory, quarantine and scratch cleanup into one unpublished constructor worker. Keep cache-budget enforcement and device release on the model thread. Preserve raw lock descriptors through partial-open failures and defer final unlock/close until every writer and startup worker drains.

Bound streamed-weight header inventory, shard opening/header checks and live fstat/path identity verification. Retain late-open descriptors and uncertain-close inventories; prevent publication when integrity checking expires.

Bound PLE manifest/content validation, startup open/fstat, preverified identity stat and hot-row-file inventory. Keep foreground and prefetch leases through late startup completion. Remove filesystem work from the fork/rebuild lock and reset that lock after fork, so blocked final close cannot trap a replacement constructor.

Bound optional expert atlas/trace bind, writes, persistence and final close. Snapshot counts on the caller thread and publish persisted-observation accounting only after success; late writes may finish on disk but never receive successful persistence credit.
Remove the exact-checkpoint close path's second direct file.close call; the I/O pool exclusively owns its one final close.
Strengthen one existing read-timeout test to await true finalizer completion rather than an event emitted inside a still-running close callback.

oracles: Caller deadlines under blocked startup open, source fstat before and after read, APC lock/security/rescan, atlas persistence, PLE hot-row inventory and descriptor close.
Actual descriptors stay open while workers still use them, close after late completion and never close twice after an fd number could be reused.
Blocked or uncertain close refuses replacement pools; a permanently blocked finalizer cannot hold interpreter exit.
Partial APC fstat/fdopen failures release the descriptor; timed-out startup never publishes an APC manager.
Late atlas persistence and PLE preheat never publish success accounting or cache entries.

limits: These are bounded caller waits, not syscall interruption. A permanently blocked worker or finalizer retains its existing owner; replacement is refused until it drains. An uncertain close error remains quarantined for the process lifetime and requires process restart rather than an unsafe retry.

The default control/startup operation deadline is 60 seconds and each final-close caller wait is 2 seconds. Existing payload, spill and metadata deadlines remain distinct. This is not one global deadline for all model construction or shutdown.
MLX evaluation, synchronization, array creation, cache release and model-thread scheduling are outside this pure-filesystem guarantee and remain on their owning thread.

Raw offline serialization/header/atlas helpers and externally supplied nonproduction executors retain their explicit synchronous behavior. General model artifact loaders outside the named cache/streaming/PLE paths are not covered by this change.

A timed-out atlas write can complete on disk after the caller reports failure; the collector is poisoned, further writes are refused and persisted-observation accounting is not advanced. No performance or route qualification claim is made.
